# 1st Kalasha International Film & TV Awards

The 1st Kalasha Film and Television Awards ceremony, presented by the Kenya Film Commission, honoured the best in Kenyan television and film for the year 2009. The awards recognize excellence in storytelling, direction, performanceand technical execution in the Kenyan entertainment industry.
Wanuri Kahiu's acclaimed film From a Whisper, based on the real-life events surrounding the 1998 US Embassy bombings in Nairobi,  won Best Film Overall. In the television categories, Jackline Nyaminde won Best Actress in a Television Series for her role in Papa Shirandula, while Mburu Kimani's The Race won Best Riverwood Film. Mumbi Maina was also recognized for her performance, taking home the Best Supporting Actress award for Unseen Unsung Unforgotten.
Background
The Kalasha Awards were established by the Kenya Film Commission to recognize and promote excellence in Kenya's film and television industry, drawing inspiration from international award systems such as the Academy Awards. The name "Kalasha" symbolizes the growth and development of the audiovisual sector in Kenya. The awards celebrate achievement, set industry standards and encourage healthy competition among practitioners.
An academy of industry professionals oversees the selection process, including nomination and judging across key filmmaking categories. Winners are determined through a mixed voting system, with 70% from the academy and 30% from public voting, while technical categories are decided solely by the academy.
Ceremony
The inaugural awards were held in June 2009 at the Crowne Plaza in Upper Hill, Nairobi, Kenya. The event was established by the Kenya Film Commission to celebrate cultural diversity through film and to motivate local producers towards high-quality film and TV productions. The 1st edition's categories were structured to formally represent the five original branches of filmmaking: directors, actors, writers, producers, and technicians.
